**Lands in `packages/objectql` / `packages/metadata-protocol`** ⇒ `domain:engine`.

**Class (b), declared-but-unenforced on an install door**: `InstallPackageRequestSchema.enableOnInstall` (`package-registry.zod.ts:283`, `z.boolean().default(true)`) is the **request contract** of the in-process `installPackage` primitive, and the door **ignores it**. ⇒ a caller who sets it gets no effect and no signal.

**`p2`** — same family as objectstack#19120 (`POST /api/v1/packages` accepting a manifest with no `version`, graded `p1` this shift), and deliberately a grade below it: #19120 is the **published HTTP** door on the golden path's install step, this is the **in-process** primitive. ⇒ narrower audience, same class.

⚠️ **The ruling context matters and the card carries it**: batch #153 item 5 letter 1 (#18605, record `5724940709`) kept that declaration as a **copy**. ⇒ the claiming seat must read that ruling before deciding whether the fix is 「honour it」 or 「stop declaring it」 — ⛔ this seat is not choosing between enforce and retire on a surface a maintainer ruling already touched.

## ⚠️⚠️ This card's stated prerequisite is MET, and its reference matrix MOVED — both measured this act

**Prerequisite met.** The card says 「Lands after PR #19130 (#18605) so the parity pin exists」. **PR #19130 is MERGED** — `596090efb` on `origin/main`, read 2026-09-20T11:15Z. ⇒ ⛔ no sequencing block remains.

**⛔ But the matrix it points at is no longer the matrix it describes.** The card (written 2026-09-20T09:06Z) says the in-process door should follow 「`enableOnInstall ?? true` on install **and on re-install**」, calling that 「the same matrix `packages-install-enable-on-install.test.ts` pins on the HTTP door」.

⭐ **This seat landed #19291 (`4fef271b71`) at 2026-09-20T11:10Z — two hours after this card was written — and it re-ruled exactly those cells.** Read on `origin/main` just now:

| line | case | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `:154` | an ABSENT `enableOnInstall` **installs** it enabled | ✅ still true — **FRESH** install |
| `:233` | **[#18877 re-ruled]** **re-installing** with the flag ABSENT **PRESERVES** the disable | ⛔ **contradicts** 「`?? true` on re-install」 |
| `:278` | **[#18877 re-ruled]** a BARE re-install **PRESERVES** it too | ⛔ same |
| `:262` | re-install with `enableOnInstall: true` clears the durable disable | ✅ still true |

⇒ the card is ⛔ **not wrong about direction** — 「honour it exactly as the HTTP door does」 is a self-updating instruction and it still governs. It is **incomplete about mechanism**: `?? true` is precisely what the HTTP door stopped doing for the re-install-absent case, under maintainer ruling batch **#157** item 5 letter C (「缺省 = 保持,有旗 = 设置」), which is **younger** than this card's own ruling (batch #153 letter 1).

⛔ **The direction wins; the mechanism sentence is spent.** The dispatch order tells the dev to take the matrix from the **test file on the tree**, ⛔ never from the card's prose.

## Fences

- ⛔ **Not `packages/spec`** — the card says so, and the declaration half is #19273's (`domain:spec`, whose `Blocked-by: #18605` is now discharged, ⛔ not this seat's to move).
- `Clause-②: no` — a runtime behaviour change behind a key **already declared**; ⛔ no accept set loosened, ⛔ no public surface widened. If the diff contradicts that, stop and report rather than re-grading.
- ⭐ The card's own measurement to re-verify, ⛔ not inherit: 「no existing caller sets the key (every HTTP-door path deliberately does not forward it), so behaviour is unchanged for every current caller」.

## ⭐ The dispatch's stale-matrix warning was taken the right way

I told this dev the card's mechanism sentence (「`?? true` on install **and re-install**」) was spent, gave it a four-row table, and said 「take the matrix from the **file**, and if your reading disagrees with mine, **follow the file and say so**」.

⇒ it re-read `packages-install-enable-on-install.test.ts` itself and reports its reading **matches cell for cell** (`:154` absent+fresh = enabled · `:233` re-install+absent = **PRESERVES** · `:262` re-install+true = clears · `:278` bare re-install = **PRESERVES**), with 「no disagreement to report」. ⭐ The implementation follows the file.

⭐⭐ **And the spelling is right for the reason that matters**: `=== true` / `=== false`, ⛔ never truthiness, ⛔ never a `?? default` — 「the three states **ARE** the contract」, so a non-boolean reads as **absent** rather than coercing. Under letter C, `?? true` would have collapsed 「absent」 into 「true」 and silently re-broken exactly what #18877 just fixed.

⭐ **The pin drives the REAL `SchemaRegistry` and the REAL protocol implementation**, with the reason stated: 「a registry double cannot tell 'the registry preserved the row' from 'the door did nothing'」. ⇒ a mock would have made the two hypotheses **indistinguishable** — the pin would pass either way. That is the difference between a test and a test-shaped object.

⭐ The card's no-op claim was **re-verified, not inherited**: the only two call sites (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts:769`, and `duplicatePackage` in the same file) both omit the key ⇒ ⛔ no live path changes behaviour.

## ⚠️⚠️ The finding that outlives this PR — filed as #19339

This PR **falsifies a published description**, and the dev flagged the rule conflict rather than silently picking a side. I re-took every reading on `origin/main`:

```
packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts   → .describe('… this protocol primitive does not read it')
content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx:1913      → same sentence, published page
content/docs/references/kernel/package-registry.mdx:187 → same sentence, published page
packages/spec/src/api/package-api.zod.ts           → a second copy in prose
```

⇒ all false once this lands. ⭐⭐ **And no gate can see it**: `check:docs` holds the generated page **equal to the `.describe()`**, and they still agree **with each other** — the instrument proves internal consistency, ⛔ not truth.

**How the conflict was resolved, recorded so it can be overruled.** 「本轮令其变假的已发布缺陷必修」 met 「新 `packages/spec` 工作恒由 `domain:spec` 席收口」. This seat landed on **file, don't breach**, because: (1) the fix is the spec lane's surface; (2) a `.describe()` edit pulls in the generated-artifact family plus a second changeset — a new verification surface; (3) ⭐ the falsity runs in the **safe direction** — the text **understates** a capability, so a reader who believes it simply does not set the key and gets the behaviour they'd have got anyway. That is the **inverse** of the project's named failure mode, ⛔ not an instance of it.

⇒ **#19339** filed (`domain:spec`, `pm:queue`), with the timing that explains it (the three copies were written by PR #19130, merged **two hours after** this card was filed — two correct changes crossed) and a note that it must be **sequenced with #19273**, which rewrites the same field's text. ⚠️ If the spec seat or the maintainer judges (3) too generous, the remedy is that card, ⛔ not a revert.

## Deviations — all declared

1. **Scope fence held at a cost, and said so** — see above. ⭐ Reporting the conflict instead of resolving it unilaterally is the behaviour the conflict rule asks for.
2. **The durable half, newly reachable**: an in-process `enableOnInstall: false` moves the registry row but ⛔ not the runtime's disable file (keyed by `environmentId`, which `InstallPackageRequest` does not carry), so a restart re-enables. ⛔ Not filable at this seam — closing it is a **contract** decision, and no caller on the tree sets the key. ⭐ Stated in the code, the changeset **and** the PR body, which is the right treatment for a gap with no carrier. I considered filing it and agreed with the dev: ⛔ no named carrier ⇒ Acceptance notes.
3. **Zero label writes** — my dispatch budget named none, and it honoured the narrower instruction over the standard clause. `api_writes` **2**, `mcp_calls` **0**.
4. `origin/main` merged mid-run because the reconciliation refused to vouch for a stale tree; the 4 incoming commits touch **no** package, and all 61 gates were re-run at the final head anyway.
5. Ablation rebuilt through `dist` before reading the colour — `packages/objectql` resolves `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` via exports with ⛔ no vitest alias, so an un-rebuilt ablation would have read green off a stale artifact. Marker proven present in 2 built files, then **absent from all 24** after restore, tree clean.

CI converging on head `2c8e2667c` (13 success · 3 skipped · 15 in progress · **0 red** at review time). Required floor unread ⇒ ⛔ no ready, ⛔ no enqueue yet. This seat carries it to MERGED.

## What is now true on `main`

`MetadataProtocol.installPackage` honours `enableOnInstall` under ruling batch #157 item 5 letter C — the same rule the HTTP door implements: `true` ⇒ enable, `false` ⇒ disable, **absent ⇒ no lifecycle call**, so a fresh id still lands at the declared default and an existing row is **preserved**. ⇒ the declared-but-inert key ADR-0049 and Prime Directive #10 refuse is enforced, ⛔ not retired (ruling batch #153 item 5 letter 1 kept the declaration as a copy with the same meaning).

⭐ Spelled `=== true` / `=== false`, ⛔ never truthiness and ⛔ never `?? true`: the three states **are** the contract, so a non-boolean reads as absent rather than coercing. Under letter C a `?? true` would have collapsed 「absent」 into 「true」 and silently re-broken what #18877 (`4fef271b71`) had just fixed.

⛔ No live path changed: the only two call sites both omit the key.

## ⚠️ As of this commit, three PUBLISHED statements are FALSE — tracked at #19339

`packages/spec/src/kernel/package-registry.zod.ts`'s `.describe()` says 「this protocol primitive does not read it」, and that sentence ships to `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx:1913` and `content/docs/references/kernel/package-registry.mdx:187`; `package-api.zod.ts` carries a second copy in prose. ⇒ **they became false at `482d584121`.**

⭐⭐ **No gate can see it**: `check:docs` holds the generated page **equal to** the `.describe()`, and they still agree with each other — the instrument proves internal consistency, ⛔ not truth.

⛔ Not fixed here by design: `packages/spec` is the `domain:spec` seat's surface, and the falsity runs in the **safe direction** (the text *understates* a capability, so a reader who believes it simply does not set the key). **#19339** carries it with an executable criterion and a note that it must be sequenced with **#19273**, which rewrites the same field's text. ⚠️ If that judgement reads as too generous, the remedy is #19339, ⛔ not a revert.
